questions.question: What specific assurances can be provided to the public regarding the allocation of the additional tax revenue from the new transient occupancy tax?
questions.answer: The speakers expressed a concern that the new tax revenue would go into the general fund without a clear commitment to fund the arts or other community projects. It was suggested that including stipulations for arts funding in the ballot measure could help address these concerns.

questions.question: How can the city council effectively communicate the benefits of the new tax measure to citizens who are already fatigued by high taxation?
questions.answer: Engaging the community and emphasizing the direct positive impact on local arts and cultural programs may help in garnering support. Transparency and clear messaging regarding the use of funds could also alleviate concerns.

questions.question: What strategies can be employed to ensure the proposed tax measure gains voter approval in March 2020?
questions.answer: The speakers indicated that a robust campaign similar to those for previous measures, involving direct outreach and education about the benefits of the measure, would be essential for gaining voter support.

questions.question: What role do local arts organizations believe they can play in promoting this tax measure to the community?
questions.answer: Local arts organizations, represented by speakers during the meeting, expressed their willingness to advocate for the measure by highlighting how the funds could revitalize the arts community and contribute to educational programs.

questions.question: How can the concerns raised by citizens regarding tax fatigue and allocation be addressed in the subsequent discussions before the election?
questions.answer: It will be important for the city council to address these concerns by providing detailed plans on how the funds will be allocated and by engaging in dialogue with the community to incorporate their feedback and questions.

Speaker 8: Good evening, Honorable Vice Mayor and Council Members. Thank you for the opportunity to present on our trauma informed systems efforts. In 2015, the Department of Health and Human Services began working with community partners to explore the possibility of becoming a trauma informed city. In 2016, the group launched Trauma and Resiliency in Forum Long Beach, also known as Tree Shelby, a citywide initiative focused on reducing the impacts of persistent trauma in organizations and across systems. This network is a group of Long Beach professionals who are committed to holding the vision, setting priorities, developing and tracking data measurements and championing a trauma informed Long Beach. I would like to share some information with you on what a trauma and resiliency informed system actually is. But I must start with defining trauma. The continuous exposure to violence, poverty and other forms of disparity can have significant impacts on communities. Trauma can be defined as a psychological, emotional response to an event or an experience that is deeply distressing or disturbing. Immediately after the event, shock and denial are typical. Longer term reactions can include unpredictable emotions, flashbacks, strained relationships, and even physical symptoms like headaches and nausea. When trauma happens, it has short term and long term effects on the individual, on families and on the overall community. For many people in Long Beach, the continuous exposure to unsafe environments has resulted in higher rates of heart disease, respiratory illness and other health related outcomes. Persistent trauma not only impacts our community members and clients, it impacts our service providers, systems and the physical environment. Places and spaces where people live, work and play. Like schools, health care facilities, faith based organizations, social services and businesses play a key role in addressing the impacts of trauma within communities. How services are offered in these spaces actually play a key role in either reducing or enhancing the effects of being exposed to this trauma for their employees and service providers. The way in which services service providers hold, process and manage trauma will in turn have an impact on the experiences of community members who are seeking services. Many of these folks are trying to navigate complex systems while caring their own traumatic load. The Health Department and others recognize that a crucial point to interrupt the cycle of retraumatize is the retraumatizing of clients. Is supporting staff in addressing the vicarious trauma they might experience regularly in the workplace? In simpler terms, when a person walks in the door who is carrying a load of trauma and the staff person providing the service doesn't understand the effects of this person may be carrying. This can sometimes cause a domino effect of unsuccessful interactions between the two that may lead to more trauma for both the client and the staff person. Vicarious trauma is the emotional and psychological impact of connecting with the traumatic life events of other people. It often occurs without awareness. It accumulates over time and can change a worker's overall view of the world and people around them. This as this often affects a person's overall health and wellbeing as well. Resiliency, on the other hand, refers to the ability to cope with hardships and adapt to challenges or change. Resiliency develops over time and gives the capacity not only to manage with life's challenges, but also to be better prepared for the next stressful situation. The ability to remain hopeful is essential to resiliency and the process of healing. A trauma informed system is one in which all people within the organization recognize and respond to the impact of trauma. Traumatic stress on those who have contact with the system, including those seeking services, and us as service providers. This initiative is designed specifically to move Long Beach to become a trauma and resiliency informed city. The goal is that over time, collectively, we will embrace a comprehensive understanding of trauma and resiliency and incorporate this into our policy and practice. The implementation of the Tri Tre Alb initiative includes three core components training and education, policy and practice, change and evaluation. The goals of the pilot are to one begin with two identified systems the Health Department and the Long Beach Public Libraries, to adopt policies and procedures that enhance the delivery of services through trauma and resiliency. Informed approaches to convene a task force to advise the development of strategies to support staff in how to deliver trauma and resiliency. Informed Care and three Document Organizational Culture shift in the processes demonstrating how services are delivered and communities engaged for future replication. The Health Department and Library staff, as well as the City of Long Beach, Human Resources Department and the City Council offices, will receive training on these practices, the impact of trauma on ourselves and our clients, and tools for building resiliency in order to mean healthy, healthy responses in our work place. Relationships, training for h.R. And City Council will be prioritized and conducted in January 2020. Training will begin for health and library staff shortly thereafter. Additionally, the Health Department and library policies and procedures will be assessed for alignment with trauma and resiliency. Informed approaches and recommendations will be made for policy change. The evaluation component is designed to help us assess how well the training promotes learning and implementation of trauma and resiliency, informed approaches and the degree to which the policy changes are effective. This concludes my presentation. I'm available for any questions. Thank you.

questions.question: What specific steps are being taken to ensure that trauma-informed practices will be integrated into services provided by the city?
questions.answer: The initiative includes training and education, policy and practice change, and evaluation. The goal is to start with the Health Department and Long Beach Public Libraries and train their staff on trauma-informed practices to improve service delivery.

questions.question: How is the city planning to address the challenges associated with hiring and filling vacancies in various departments?
questions.answer: The city has engaged in an in-depth analysis of the hiring process, highlighting the importance of collaboration among stakeholders, streamlining processes, and targeting recruitment efforts to expedite filling positions.

questions.question: What are the recommendations regarding medical screenings in the city's hiring process?
questions.answer: The audit suggests that the city should perform a cost-benefit analysis regarding the necessity of medical screenings for all employees, noting that Long Beach is one of the few cities that requires such screenings universally, which can impede hiring.

questions.question: Is there an exploration of a cannabis policy for city employees given its legalization?
questions.answer: The city is currently exploring the implications of medical marijuana in the workplace, weighing potential policies against existing DOJ guidelines, particularly regarding which positions may still require medical testing.

questions.question: How will the newly proposed onboarding processes for employees and elected officials be standardized?
questions.answer: The audit recommends that the city develop a written onboarding policy that includes clear roles, responsibilities, and expectations, as well as standardize informal performance check-ins and establish exit interview policies to improve onboarding and employee retention.

questions.question: What specific steps does Councilwoman Price propose to ease the fears of homeless individuals regarding their belongings when accepting services?
questions.answer: Councilwoman Price proposes the creation of dedicated teams that can inventory, collect, transport, and store the property of homeless individuals, allowing them to accept services without the fear of losing their belongings.

questions.question: How does the proposal intend to improve the efficiency of city staff working with homeless individuals?
questions.answer: The proposal aims to free up existing city staff who currently spend long periods inventorying property, allowing them to focus more on providing services to homeless individuals.

questions.question: What are some of the potential challenges mentioned regarding getting homeless individuals to accept help?
questions.answer: One of the challenges mentioned is that many individuals experiencing homelessness are reluctant to accept help because they do not want to part with their belongings, which they feel is a significant loss.

questions.question: In what ways is the proposed inventory team expected to support existing outreach efforts?
questions.answer: The inventory team is expected to support existing outreach efforts by ensuring that individuals can keep their belongings safe while they transition into services, thereby increasing the likelihood that they will accept help.

questions.question: What specific steps are being taken to help the College of Instrument Technology secure a new relocation site?
questions.answer: The city is working with the College of Instrument Technology and already has begun discussions with the California State Bureau of Postsecondary Education regarding the move. However, a confirmed training site is needed before further actions can be taken.

questions.question: How was the relocation budget determined for the affected businesses, particularly for the College of Instrument Technology?
questions.answer: The relocation estimates included in the plan are based on a general assessment of current conditions, and once a suitable site is located, actual costs will be assessed in collaboration with the Overland Pacific Cutler consultants.

questions.question: What challenges are the current tenants facing as they prepare for their relocation?
questions.answer: Current tenants are concerned about the lack of a confirmed relocation site and sufficient funding to cover moving their specialized equipment and ensuring continuity of their programs.

questions.question: What is the significance of the training programs offered by the College of Instrument Technology to the local community?
questions.answer: The programs provide critical job training to underserved populations, including veterans and the unemployed, leading to high employment rates and better opportunities for many graduates.

questions.question: How does the council plan to address the funding concerns raised by the speakers during public comment?
questions.answer: The council expressed a commitment to ensuring fair communication and support for the tenants, particularly emphasizing the need to adequately address relocation costs and assist in securing a new site.

questions.question: How will the proposed 1% increase in the transient occupancy tax specifically benefit the arts and culture sector in Long Beach?
questions.answer: The increase is expected to generate approximately $2.8 million annually, which will provide stable funding for arts education programs, community arts initiatives, local museums, theaters, and support operational costs associated with the Convention Center.

questions.question: What measures are being implemented to ensure that the increase in tax will not negatively impact Long Beach residents?
questions.answer: The tax will only be levied on guests renting hotel rooms, motels, or short-term rentals, meaning Long Beach residents who do not utilize these accommodations will not be paying this tax.

questions.question: Can you elaborate on the challenges faced by arts organizations in Long Beach that this funding seeks to address?
questions.answer: Many arts organizations struggle with fluctuating attendance and donations, making financial stability difficult. This proposed increase will provide a consistent revenue source to support their operations and educational outreach efforts.

questions.question: What steps are being taken to ensure transparency on how the funds generated from the tax will be allocated?
questions.answer: It was mentioned that part of the proposal includes discussions around how the funds will be structured and allocated specifically for arts, culture, and the convention center, ensuring that these funds are directed towards the intended purposes.

questions.question: How does the proposed transient occupancy tax increase compare to similar taxes in other cities?
questions.answer: Currently, Long Beach's transient occupancy tax is at 12%, while the proposed increase would bring it to 13%. Comparatively, cities like Anaheim charge up to 15%, while others range from 10% to 17%, indicating that the increase keeps Long Beach competitive.

questions.question: What steps has been taken to address concerns about the environmental impacts raised against the proposed project, particularly regarding air quality?
questions.answer: The applicant's representative stated that the project complied with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and that an addendum was deemed appropriate by the city based on an extensive review. They assert that no substantial new environmental impacts exist beyond those analyzed in the downtown plan's programmatic environmental impact report (EIR).

questions.question: How does the project align with the community's needs for affordable housing, as expressed by various stakeholders?
questions.answer: Stakeholders, including the North Pine Neighborhood Alliance, expressed that the project does not meet the need for affordable and low-cost rental housing, emphasizing the necessity for such housing in the downtown area, especially given rising market rates.

questions.question: What specific mitigation measures have been proposed to address the indoor air quality concerns mentioned during the hearing?
questions.answer: The appellant suggested that the project should require the use of no-formaldehyde-added materials to reduce potential health risks from indoor air quality, which the applicant acknowledged but contradicted by arguing that the project's compliance with existing air quality regulations would mitigate such risks.

questions.question: Given the concerns about traffic and parking raised by residents, what measures are in place to handle the expected increase in population and vehicles from the project?

questions.question: What specific changes to the ordinance was Councilwoman Price advocating for during the meeting?
questions.answer: Councilwoman Price requested changes to ban flavored vapor products while excluding traditional tobacco products like cigars, chewing tobacco, and pipe tobacco from the ban. She also suggested incorporating language emphasizing diversion and education for minors and increasing minimum civil penalties.

questions.question: What urgent public health issue is being addressed with the proposed temporary ban on flavored vaping products?
questions.answer: The proposed ban aims to mitigate youth consumption of flavored vaping products, which are linked to an increase in nicotine addiction and respiratory health concerns, as well as potential pulmonary injuries connected to vaping.

questions.question: Why was there a discussion about including menthol tobacco products in the ban?
questions.answer: Menthol tobacco products were included in discussions because they are recognized as particularly enticing to youth, similar to flavored vaping products, and there is concern that they contribute to nicotine addiction among this demographic.

questions.question: How did the council plan to approach the public health concerns related to vaping products moving forward?
questions.answer: The council plans to implement the temporary ban on flavored vaping products while allowing time for further research and discussion about the health implications of these products. They aim to monitor federal regulations and gather data over the year to shape future policy.

questions.question: What concerns did some speakers express about equipping local businesses to comply with the ordinance?
questions.answer: Some speakers expressed worries that the ban might push customers to neighboring cities, adversely affecting local businesses while highlighting the importance of responsible retail practices to prevent youth access to nicotine products.

questions.question: What are the immediate steps proposed to restore basic life support units 12 and 13 to daily service?
questions.answer: The city manager is requested to explore and implement solutions to restore bills 12 and 13 to daily service as soon as possible and prepare a long-term plan to address staffing shortages.

questions.question: What challenges related to staffing levels have been identified in the Long Beach Fire Department?
questions.answer: The Long Beach Fire Department is experiencing staffing shortages for ambulance operator positions due to limited candidates completing the hiring process and competition for personnel among other fire departments.

questions.question: How does the disparity between Advanced Life Support (ALS) and Basic Life Support (BLS) services affect patient care in Long Beach?
questions.answer: ALS services handle critical cases requiring immediate intervention, while BLS services are responsible for transporting patients who do not need urgent medical attention, potentially leading to longer response times if BLS units are insufficient.

questions.question: What measures are being considered to improve the hiring process for ambulance operators in the Long Beach Fire Department?
questions.answer: The city plans to work with civil service and HR to better plan hiring academies, and to explore options for additional support or maintaining a pool of qualified candidates to avoid staffing shortages.

questions.question: What long-term strategies will be implemented to prevent future staffing shortages for ambulance services?
questions.answer: The council is exploring methods to streamline the hiring process, review compensation to make positions more competitive, and potentially reintroduce supplemental or contract ambulance services during peak demands.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the urgency ordinance being discussed?
questions.answer: The primary purpose of the urgency ordinance is to prohibit no fault evictions and no fault notices through December 31, 2019, in response to the pending implementation of the Tenant Protection Act, which is intended to protect tenants from sudden rent increases and evictions.

questions.question: How does the timing of the proposed ordinance relate to the Tenant Protection Act?
questions.answer: The timing is crucial because the Tenant Protection Act goes into effect on January 1, 2020. There is a gap between the announcement of the Act and its implementation, during which landlords may issue 60-day eviction notices to evict tenants before the new protections kick in.

questions.question: What unresolved issues did speakers raise regarding the impacts of the recent rental market changes?
questions.answer: Speakers raised concerns regarding the unfairness of evictions occurring during the holiday season, the emotional toll on families being displaced, and the need for enhanced communication and education about tenants' rights and the validity of eviction notices.

questions.question: What proactive measures does the council plan to take following the vote on the ordinance?
questions.answer: The council plans to conduct education outreach to inform tenants and landlords about the new laws and how they intersect with local ordinances, along with potential future discussions on strengthening tenant protections.

questions.question: What happens to the tenants who have received relocation payments if they choose to stay in their homes after the ordinance passes?
questions.answer: If tenants who have received half of their relocation payments choose to stay in their homes after the ordinance passes, they must reimburse the landlords for those payments, as failure to do so could be grounds for eviction.

questions.question: What were the key provisions of the tentative agreement reached with the Long Beach Firefighters Association?
questions.answer: The agreement includes a three-year contract with general salary increases of 3% in the first year, 3% at the start of the third year, and 3% six months later. It also features a one-time payment of $2,000 in the second year, adjustments related to CalPERS pension reform, bilingual skill pay increase, a new hazmat first responder operations pay, modifications to current skill pays, a new parental leave program, and agreements for a joint committee to address behavioral health benefits.

questions.question: How does the new parental leave program benefit firefighters and their families?
questions.answer: The new parental leave program offers firefighters a supportive family medical leave, which is crucial for the many young firefighters who are starting families. This reflects the city's commitment to maintaining a healthy work-life balance for its employees.

questions.question: What impact do the negotiations and the new contract have on the recruitment and retention of firefighters in Long Beach?
questions.answer: The fair and competitive contract, along with the benefits it provides, is expected to help retain and recruit qualified fire service professionals, particularly in a competitive Southern California job market where agencies are vying for the same talent.

questions.question: How are mental health support and other benefits addressed in this new agreement for firefighters?
questions.answer: The agreement includes plans to convene a Joint Labor Management Committee to discuss issues related to behavioral health benefits and services provided through the Employee Assistance Plan, aiming to improve mental health support for firefighters.

questions.question: What measures will be taken to track the effectiveness of the childcare pilot program over its 12-month duration?
questions.answer: The pilot program will track how many people from outside the city are using the childcare services, how many city employees utilize them, and the overall effectiveness based on the number of hours requested and the feedback from participants.

questions.question: Given the initial funding of $3,000, how will the program be sustained if demand exceeds expectations?
questions.answer: If the allocated funds run out before the end of the pilot period, the council will reevaluate and discuss further funding options to ensure the program's continuation.

questions.question: Will the childcare services provided during council meetings be licensed, and how will the quality of care be ensured?
questions.answer: Yes, the childcare service will be provided by licensed caretakers who have met all necessary requirements, including insurance and safety regulations, to ensure a safe environment for children.

questions.question: How will the city ensure equal access to childcare services for both public attendees and city employees during meetings?
questions.answer: The childcare services will be completely free for both the public members and city employees during council meetings, allowing equal access to all attendees.

questions.question: What considerations are being made for potentially expanding childcare services beyond council meetings in the future?
questions.answer: Stakeholders have expressed interest in exploring the possibility of developing a more comprehensive childcare facility that could serve city employees and the public, especially as development plans for the area progress.

And before I get too far into it, I want to take this opportunity to to thank your city clerk, Monique Della Garza, and her staff, who have been absolutely integral partners with us throughout this process. And we could not be where we're at with the success of this effort and with the hard work that still remains ahead without without her support and all the work that she's done. So thank you, Monique, for that. So I'm very pleased to share with you that that after ten years of of work and research and engagement with the public, that we are ready to move towards a revolutionized form of voting in Los Angeles County. And when I say revolutionized, I'm talking about the voting experience we have in Los Angeles County from the perspective of a voter walking into a voting location on Election Day. The voting experience really hasn't changed since 1968, when punch card voting was first unrolled here in Los Angeles County. A lot of things behind the scenes have changed and updated since then, but from that voter experience, it really has remained the same and a lot has changed since 1968. And it is time for new opportunities, new options and new choices for voters in that voting experience. And we hope that through the work that we've done that, that we're doing this in a way that is going to increase participation, but also live up to the significance of that voting experience for our 5.4 million registered voters in Los Angeles County. I only have a brief period of time this evening, so I'll focus on on the significant elements of that change in voter experience. So gone will be the single day, single location, voting on a random Tuesday between 7 a.m. and 8 p.m.. And we're moving towards a vote center model where voters in Los Angeles County can go to any vote center in the county over a period of 11 days to cast their ballot, which means we will have two full weekends of voting and we will give voters the opportunity to choose to vote at a location that is either convenient or more significant to them. So if it's easier for them to vote close to their home, we'll have vote centers in that area. If it's easier for them to vote somewhere close to work, somewhere close to where they drop their children off at school, or somewhere where they go shopping on the weekends. That the idea here is to be present in the community and to meet people where they are. And so so if they watched a debate on television the night before and they feel engaged and they feel like they're ready to cast their vote, that while they're out in their community, they will see a place that's available for them to do that. So the vote centers are really the most significant change in that that allows voters to vote anywhere will open those starting 11 days before the election, four days before the election will increase that to a larger number of locations. And again, those are available anywhere in the county at those vote centers. You will also be able to register to vote and vote on the same day. You can update your voter registration. So if you had an address change or if you had a change in party preference, you will have the opportunity to make those changes as well, drastically reducing the the need for provisional ballots, which often extend the canvass period in our elections process. So we're very pleased to be able to offer that. The way that we will be able to do that is through the use of an electronic pullback. So when voters arrive at these vote centers, they will check in using an electronic tablet poll book. We will be able to access all registered voters in the county. This is also our security mechanism so that if you do go vote somewhere close to work and then you try to go vote somewhere close to home, we will know that you have already voted and and we will be able to prevent any any attempts to vote more than once. They this will replace the paper roster. So you may recall in 2018 we had some issues with our paper rosters in L.A. County. One of the great things about this model is over that 11 day period, it really gives us a better opportunity to to recover and respond to any unexpected conditions that might happen during the election process. Another feature that we will unroll that we're very excited about is an interactive sample ballot, and this is an option that will be available to all voters. It's option. It's not required. But just as we mail everybody a paper sample ballot, we will now make the sample ballot available as an electronic app that you can download on your personal device or access through our website. You can then go through your process and press make your preselections by marking those on your electronic sample ballot. Take that with you to the vote center, scan it into the voting device, and it'll pre populate your choices so that you can print your ballot and have an expedited voting experience. We think that's a game changer for voters who are used to interacting with their personal devices. It still allows for the security because the ballot that you cast at the vote center is that. Paper ballot that's produced app on the device. You can change your mind at that point. But we also know with all of the consolidation of elections, with the local districts and municipalities now on the even year cycle, that our ballot is going to be very long, especially in March and the presidential primary. It's going to be a long ballot. So the ability for voters to have that option, to have an expedited voting experience is particularly important. That ballot marking device that you will encounter at our vote centers is that is been a labor of service and a labor of love on this project. It is designed truly to be a voting solution for all people, meaning that that voters with disabilities can use the same voting device that all voters use. They will no longer be relegated to a single device in the back of the room that that the poll workers are less familiar with. Everybody will vote on the same device. questions.question: What specific changes to the voting experience are being implemented in Los Angeles County for the 2020 election cycle?
questions.answer: Los Angeles County is introducing a vote center model allowing voters to vote at any location in the county over an 11-day period, including two full weekends of voting. Voters can register and vote on the same day, and an electronic poll book will be used to streamline the process.

questions.question: How will the new electronic poll book enhance security and voting efficiency?
questions.answer: The electronic poll book will track registered voters and their voting status, preventing individuals from voting multiple times. It replaces the previous paper roster system that had issues in the 2018 election.

questions.question: What strategies are in place to ensure that voters are aware of the new voting options and processes?
questions.answer: There is a four-month public education and outreach campaign, including a demonstration center and street teams in the community to inform voters about the new voting system and its benefits.

questions.question: How do the new voting machines accommodate voters with disabilities?
questions.answer: The new voting devices are designed for all voters, including those with disabilities, allowing customization in usage with features like audio capability, tactile keypads, and adjustable touch screens.

questions.question: In what ways is the community being involved in honoring women during the suffrage celebration?
questions.answer: The Long Beach Suffrage 100 group is collecting nominations to honor women of significance in each district and will bring forth recommendations to the city council throughout the year.

questions.answer: The new owner, Stuart Nakahara, stated that they are working to improve the restroom access by changing the traffic flow for patrons to direct them away from the front door of Marina Wine, and toward clearly marked restrooms upstairs. He noted that signage to indicate this would be enhanced to prevent confusion.

questions.question: What broader issues is the city addressing in relation to the developments in the area around Marina Wine?
questions.answer: The city is actively working on addressing conflicts arising from increased activity in the area, focusing on parking issues and restroom access for both patrons and boaters, as the popularity and number of businesses have grown.

questions.question: What was Councilman Price's stance regarding the handling of entertainment permits and business operations in the area?
questions.answer: Councilman Price emphasized the importance of treating all businesses fairly in terms of entertainment permits and compliance with city rules, expressing her intention to monitor the situation closely and work with the city manager to ensure swift responses to any complaints about noise or other issues.

questions.question: What are the specific challenges faced with the compliance of food trucks regarding the polystyrene ordinance?
questions.answer: The challenges with permitted special events mostly center around food trucks that are given their licenses outside of Long Beach and aren't made aware of the ordinance.

questions.question: What potential economic impact studies were conducted to assess the burden on small businesses due to the new ordinance?
questions.answer: A formal study was not commissioned, but some research on cost comparisons was gathered, indicating that the cost differences vary significantly based on the alternatives chosen by businesses.

questions.question: Given that no one has applied for the hardship exemption, what outreach was conducted to ensure businesses were aware of this option?
questions.answer: Businesses were made aware of the hardship exemption during visits and it was included in the outreach materials, though it wasn't discussed in all visits.

questions.question: Are there plans to expand the ban on polystyrene to include retail sales of cups and plates in addition to ice chests?
questions.answer: Currently, the ban includes retail sales of ice chests and certain products like foam balls, but expanding it to cups and plates could be considered if the council chooses to do so.

questions.question: What strategies are being implemented to promote the 'bring your own Long Beach' campaign, and how successful has it been?
questions.answer: The campaign has included the distribution of reusable items and outreach that encourages residents to use their own containers, with approximately 4000 residents pledging to utilize the reusable items.

questions.question: What alternatives to plastic straws were discussed, and how could they address the needs of individuals with disabilities?
questions.answer: Councilman Ringa mentioned alternatives like metal straws that fold easily into pockets and reusable options, and emphasized the need to find alternatives to plastic that still meet the needs of individuals with disabilities.

questions.question: How can the timeline for phasing out plastic straws and implementing the new ordinance be structured to allow businesses to adapt?
questions.answer: Councilmember Price suggested a phased approach where businesses could phase out their plastic straws while still allowing them to use their existing stock for a set period, such as six months.

questions.question: What role does public outreach play in the proposed amendments to the food packaging ordinance?
questions.answer: Councilmember Ringa noted that staff is working on a memo that will encapsulate outreach strategies and successes related to the ordinance, implying that community education and involvement are crucial for effective implementation.

questions.question: What considerations are being made for the recycling and waste management implications of banning plastic straws and food packaging?
questions.answer: The conversation highlighted that recyclable commodities have lost value, and the city is investigating changes to curbside programs to better manage waste, indicating that the proposed amendments align with broader waste management goals.

questions.question: In what ways can other environmentally friendly alternatives to straws, like those made from corn or apples, be explored and incorporated?
questions.answer: Councilmember Mongo mentioned a discussion about exploring different materials for straws, citing experiences from the Oakland airport where mass purchasing led to lower costs for sustainable straw options.

questions.question: What specific actions will be taken by the City Manager and Public Works Department regarding the infected magnolia trees, and what is the timeline for these actions?
questions.answer: The City Manager will work with the Public Works Department to return to the council with a two-from-four memorandum and a presentation within 90 days. This will include an inventory of magnolia trees, treatment recommendations, and cost assessments.

questions.question: How will community engagement be incorporated into the response plan for the magnolia tree issue?
questions.answer: Councilmember Price mentioned plans for a community meeting in the Alamitos Heights neighborhood to educate residents on the issue, providing updates and recommendations for living near affected trees.

questions.question: What preventative measures can residents take to protect their magnolia trees from the scale disease?
questions.answer: The plan will include providing residents with information on preventive maintenance for their trees, particularly for those that are currently healthy.

questions.question: What funding has been set aside to address the magnolia tree issue, and how will it be utilized?
questions.answer: Funding has already been set aside during the budget process to support efforts in managing the tree scale issue once a solution is determined.

questions.question: How prevalent is the magnolia scale infestation across the city, and what additional areas are being affected?
questions.answer: The issue has been reported in multiple districts, with increasing calls from neighborhoods noting similar sap issues in their magnolia trees, indicating it may be a growing citywide problem.

questions.question: What were the specific community benefits highlighted by supporters of the Breakers Hotel project during the hearing?
questions.answer: Supporters emphasized environmental protections, community-serving uses, and improvements to local parks, including funding for a new park and renovations to Victory Park, as key benefits of the project.

questions.question: Why is there concern regarding the difference in the economic subsidy agreement for the Breakers Hotel compared to the American Life Project?
questions.answer: The Breakers Hotel proposal was seeking a cap of $13 million for a $37 million feasibility gap, translating to 34%, while the American Life Project received a larger agreement of 28 million for a 47 million gap, which is roughly 57%.

questions.question: How does the Breakers Hotel project aim to ensure it maintains a high standard over the duration of its operation?
questions.answer: The project includes a requirement for annual certification from AAA to confirm the hotel maintains a four-diamond rating, ensuring ongoing quality and service standards.

questions.question: What is the projected economic impact of the Breakers Hotel in terms of new jobs and revenue for the city?
questions.answer: The project is expected to create approximately 500 new construction jobs and 240 permanent jobs, with projected revenues to the city totaling around $66.8 million over time.

questions.question: What stipulations are included regarding the financial arrangement for the development costs of the Breakers Hotel?
questions.answer: The developer is required to invest a minimum of $7.7 million and operate a four-diamond rated hotel for at least 20 years to ensure the city's investment is protected.

questions.question: What challenges do residents face when transitioning from homelessness to stable housing, and how does the Villages at Cabrillo support them?
questions.answer: Residents face challenges such as PTSD, mental health issues, substance abuse, and the overall trauma of homelessness. The Villages at Cabrillo provides intensive case management and support systems to help residents adjust to being housed, become good tenants, and manage daily life tasks.

questions.question: Can you elaborate on the partnerships that make the Villages at Cabrillo's services effective?
questions.answer: The Villages at Cabrillo operates in collaboration with various partners, including the City’s Health and Human Services, over 14 partner agencies, and the support of city departments like Parks and Recreation and Housing Development Services. These partnerships enhance the effectiveness of their services in addressing the needs of residents.

questions.question: What are the goals for the upcoming year as mentioned in the social impact report presentation?
questions.answer: The goals include improving outcomes for children aged zero to five who reside at the Villages at Cabrillo and ensuring that the organizational culture is responsive to the needs of the community’s residents.

questions.question: How does the Villages at Cabrillo measure its success and impact on residents’ lives?
questions.answer: Success is measured by data showing housing retention rates, with 98% of residents maintaining housing for six months and 95% for a year. Additionally, improvements in residents' lives in terms of increased income, safety, and overall well-being are key indicators of impact.

questions.question: Could you provide more information about the 2019 Social Impact Report's theme 'Whatever It Takes'?
questions.answer: The theme 'Whatever It Takes' highlights the dedication of service providers and case managers at the Villages at Cabrillo, illustrating their commitment to supporting residents in overcoming barriers to maintain housing and achieve stability.

questions.question: What new approach is being requested by Councilmember Price regarding the city attorney's involvement with the L.A. County Amicus in the Martin vs. City of Boise case?
questions.answer: Councilmember Price is requesting the city attorney to prepare a resolution in support of L.A. County's decision to file an amicus brief, as the deadline to submit a brief at the petition stage has already passed.

questions.question: How does the Ninth Circuit Court's ruling in Martin vs. City of Boise impact the city's ability to manage homelessness and enforce certain ordinances?
questions.answer: The ruling has fundamentally changed the way municipalities can enforce anti-camping ordinances, stating that they cannot prohibit public camping unless they can provide acceptable shelter to every unhoused person in their jurisdiction, severely limiting the city's ability to address homelessness.

questions.question: What are some of the tools the city currently lacks in dealing with homelessness according to the discussion?
questions.answer: The main tool currently lacking is the ability to enforce camping ordinances without having available shelter beds, which creates a situation where the city cannot act against individuals camping in public spaces unless offered services.

questions.question: Why are some council members concerned about criminalizing homelessness when discussing the local enforcement of ordinances?
questions.answer: Some council members express that enforcing laws against camping without providing shelter essentially criminalizes homelessness, which raises civil rights concerns and can exacerbate the challenges faced by homeless individuals.

questions.question: What alternative measures were discussed by council members to address homelessness beyond enforcement action?
questions.answer: Council members discussed the importance of increasing the number of shelter beds, adopting more compassionate outreach approaches, and enhancing partnerships with health services to provide assistance without resorting to criminalization.

questions.question: What measures are being implemented to ensure that public records requests remain accessible while maintaining officer privacy?
questions.answer: Staff will enhance the public records request system to clearly present options for both anonymous and identified submissions, ensuring that users can easily choose their preferred method without confusion concerning anonymity.

questions.question: How does Section 9 of the new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) potentially undermine Senate Bill 1421 regarding police transparency?
questions.answer: Section 9 allows officers to be notified of public records requests, including the requester’s name and organization, which critics argue could lead to intimidation and discourage community members from filing requests.

questions.question: What provisions exist to address concerns about retaliation against individuals requesting public records?
questions.answer: Currently, there are policies in place that prohibit using information about who requested public records to intimidate or retaliate against them, classifying any such action as misconduct subject to disciplinary measures.

questions.question: Will the city be considering changes to the public records request process based on the concerns raised during the meeting?
questions.answer: Yes, the council has expressed interest in revising the public records request process to make it more user-friendly and to enhance anonymity features, ensuring the public feels safer submitting requests.

questions.question: What are the implications of the recent changes in the Police Officers Association contract, particularly regarding the pension plan?
questions.answer: The recent contract includes a pension cost-sharing provision where classic safety employees will increase their contributions, which is intended to help alleviate some of the city’s financial burdens related to pension liabilities.

Over the past few years, CalPERS has implemented several changes to its investment strategy, an expected return designed to address the plan's unfunded liabilities and to ensure its long term fiscal sustainability. First, CalPERS adopted changes to its amortization and rate smoothing policy, which began to impact our FY 16 budget. The new rate smoothing approach is intended to eliminate the city's unfunded liability. Back then, it was in 30 years, but also exposes the city to a higher volatility in annual costs. Second, CalPERS also changed the demographic assumptions which began to impact the F.B.I. 17 budget assumptions such as mortality reflected a population that is living longer and thus collecting pension benefits over longer periods of time. Third, the board adopted a new risk mitigation strategy, which was originally slated to impact the FY18 budget. The board felt that their current investment strategy was too volatile with too much risk. So the risk mitigation strategy was implemented to slowly, over time, make the city's investment mix more conservative. Then in December 2016, CalPERS voted to lower the actuarial assumed investment rate, also known as the discount rate from the current 7.5% to 7% over three years. With the first year impacting our FY19 rates, this was done to reflect the expectation of the lower rate of returns over time. Predicted by CalPERS investment advisors for the calculation impacting our Fy20 budget. The discount rate assumption was lowered to 7.25%. The full impact of this change will be realized in Fy21 when the discount rate drops to 7%. At this time, the risk mitigation strategy was put on hold until the end of the three year period, lowering the discount rate and is slated to start back up for FY 21. Finally, most recently in 2018, CalPERS adopted changes to their amortization policy. Currently, investment gains or losses are amortized over 30 years, but this new change will shorten that period to 20 years and will start to impact our fy22 rates. The projections you see in this presentation and also included in the FY 20 adopted budget now factors in all of these changes. To address the challenge of rising pension costs. Several pension reform initiatives have been implemented both by the city and the state. Without these proactive initiatives, the city situation would have been much worse. In 2006, the city lowered the benefit formula for miscellaneous employees, also through negotiations and with the partnership of our bargaining units. By 514, all employees began paying their full employee contribution rate, which had previously been partly subsidized by the city. Then Peprah was passed by the state, which implemented new benefit formulas and new contribution requirements for employees hired on or after January 1st, 2013. Then in FY14, the city created and funded the CalPERS Stabilization Fund. This fund was an innovative approach to addressing some of the challenges we had with budget planning. This fund, however, has been discontinued as the most recent risk mitigation approach adopted by CalPERS PERS has made it unlikely that this fund will be replenished in the way that it was originally envisioned. And lastly, the city made a decision to make an early payment of the unfunded liability portion for FY 18. This was done again for the FY19 and FY 20 budgets. The FY 20 adopted budget now is estimated to save approximately 1.7 million to the general fund and 2.8 million all funds. All of these changes made by CalPERS put the city on a path to pay down its unfunded liability and strengthens the long term sustainability of the fund. However, this has also meant significant cost increases for the city over the past few years. Our pension cost increases in the general fund has been a significant cost driver. The good news is, while the costs are expected to continue to increase, the rate of growth is expected to slow and then peak in FY 31 and then start to actually decrease slowly thereafter. This table reflects the employer contribution rate as a percentage of payroll for safety and miscellaneous employees. As you can see, the rates are anticipated to grow until 531. Pension costs at these levels will be and has been a challenge to fund. But this is putting us on the right track towards paying down our unfunded liabilities and being in a better fiscal position to meet our obligations. And as mentioned before, after 531, our costs are projected to go down. Investment returns have an impact on the pension costs. So an important point to recognize is that even when investment returns are good, with all of the changes that CalPERS has made, our costs will still be expected to increase. Additionally, in the years beyond Fy21, because of the new risk mitigation methodology adopted by CalPERS, any significant gains the city experiences will partially be used to further lower the investment mix to be less risky by lowering the assumed rate of return rather than reflecting reduced costs for the city. Pension costs are not our only unfunded liability. There are three other major employer related unfunded liabilities, including retiree sick leave to pay retiree health insurance premiums, retiree health insurance subsidies and workers compensation. The city currently has 1.4 billion in these unfunded liabilities summarized in the table. Unfunded liabilities are cost for services already delivered but not paid for in full. The principal causes are generally lower than expected investment earnings on system assets, benefit enhancements that were made retroactive, and underfunding the amounts of the unfunded liabilities will vary from year to year based on these factors. For pension, the city will be again on track to pay off the unfunded pension liability. Now, in approximately 25 years for the miscellaneous plan, it is 76.4% funded and for the safety plan, it is 80.7% unfunded. The city with the support and leadership of the Mayor and City Council has worked hard over the past few years to implement strong financial policies and strategies to address these unfunded liabilities. We will continue to look for cost control strategies, explore ways to increase pension funding, and continue to adhere to strong financial policies that will keep us on track with recognizing and addressing our unfunded liabilities. And lastly, before I close, I wanted to address some common misperceptions regarding the city's pension plan that was requested by the BBC. One misperception is that pension benefit formulas continue to be very high to employees with no change or no reform that has been done. The reality is, with the state pension reform benefit, plans were also significantly reduced for new employees, and contributions that they are required to pay has increased. The miscellaneous formula is 2% at 62 for Pepper employees, and the safety formula is 2.7 at 57. As more employees become pepper, employees cost to the city will continue to decrease. Another misperception is that pension costs are increasing again, because benefits are increasing. And I just want to reiterate that pension benefits have not increased and rather decreased for new employees, and pension costs are increasing because we are working to pay down our unfunded liabilities and because of the various changes implemented by CalPERS as described in this presentation. Another misperception is that employees pay nothing towards their pension. The reality is employees pay a contribution rate required by CalPERS for classic employees safety, pay 9% of their principal wage, and miscellaneous employees pay 8% of the principal wage. And after the state reform that took effect in 2013, Peprah employees pay 50% of the normal cost rate for safety employees. That's currently 12% of their principal wage. And for miscellaneous, that's 6.5% of their principal wage. And lastly, another misperception is that the city will be paying these higher pension costs forever with no solution or end in sight. And while it is true that costs have been high, as noted in the presentation, we are on a path to pay down our unfunded liabilities. questions.question: What strategies are being considered to further increase pension funding and potentially reduce costs?
questions.answer: We are exploring different options and working with our consultants and CalPERS contacts to identify ways cities can potentially pay into a trust or pay down their unfunded liabilities early. However, we are cautious about potential unintended consequences or risks associated with these strategies.

questions.question: How does the recent change in CalPERS' investment strategy impact the city's budget projections for the next several years?
questions.answer: The changes implemented by CalPERS, including adjustments to the discount rate and amortization policy, affect the city's pension costs and overall budget projections by increasing liabilities and costs initially. However, the rate of growth in these costs is expected to slow and peak around FY31, after which a decrease is anticipated.

questions.question: What measures has the city taken to address other unfunded liabilities aside from pensions?
questions.answer: The city has recognized three other significant unfunded liabilities, including retiree sick leave, health insurance premiums, and workers' compensation. We are working to implement strategies that not only address pension obligations but also consider the funding frames for these other liabilities.

questions.question: What role does economic development play in the city's strategy to manage and pay down its unfunded liabilities?
questions.answer: Economic development is critical, and there is a desire to intentionally grow revenue in a way that prioritizes setting aside funds for unfunded liabilities rather than just funding new projects. A plan is needed to ensure that any new revenue can be allocated effectively towards these obligations.

questions.question: What measures are being taken to manage the backlog of critical technology projects due to the focus on the new Civic Center and the LBE Coast project?
questions.answer: The Technology and Innovation Department is prioritizing the LBE Coast project while also acknowledging a significant backlog of other critical technology projects. They will be addressing these future projects as staffing levels and resources allow.

questions.question: How is the Technology and Innovation Department ensuring digital inclusion for the diverse communities in Long Beach?
questions.answer: They initiated the co-creation of a digital inclusion roadmap with community stakeholders, focusing on enhancing access to technology and ensuring all residents can engage equally with city services.

questions.question: Will the new CRM system improve access to city services for non-English speakers?
questions.answer: Yes, the new Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system aims to be compliant with language access policies, providing tools for communication in multiple languages to better serve residents.

questions.question: What steps are being taken to improve the hiring process and speed up the testing for potential city employees?
questions.answer: The Civil Service Department is working to streamline the recruitment process, including communication with candidates and evaluating testing methodologies to ensure candidates receive timely updates about their application status.

questions.question: What are the main changes introduced by the streamlining ordinance regarding the order of items discussed in city council meetings?
questions.answer: The main changes include moving the consent calendar to immediately follow the Pledge of Allegiance, followed by ceremonial presentations. If an item is pulled from the consent calendar, it becomes the first item on the regular agenda.

questions.question: How does the ordinance affect the limits of debate during city council meetings?

questions.question: What does the passage of this ordinance imply for the conduct during hearings in city council?

questions.question: What specific features will the proposed app include to assist first responders with locating available resources for the homeless?
questions.answer: The app is expected to include real-time information on bed availability and services not only in Long Beach but also in the surrounding region, allowing first responders to quickly access resources such as shelters, detox beds, food banks, and other support services.

questions.question: How can the app integrate with both public and private resources to enhance its effectiveness?
questions.answer: The city intends to work with the app developer to ensure that both nonprofit and government-based resources are included in the system, as well as private providers such as hospitals and rehabilitation centers, to create a comprehensive resource network.

questions.question: What considerations are being discussed regarding privacy and data security for the vulnerable homeless population using this app?
questions.answer: Councilmembers are concerned about privacy issues, emphasizing the need for strict guidelines to protect the data of homeless individuals and ensure that the app only serves professionals who can provide help without exposing sensitive information.

questions.question: What lessons can be learned from the pilot programs in other cities like Los Angeles when implementing this app in Long Beach?
questions.answer: Long Beach can learn from Los Angeles’s experience with their app, which has successfully improved outreach by providing first responders with immediate access to available services and allowing them to build trust with the homeless population through timely assistance.

questions.question: What ongoing support and resources will be necessary to keep the app updated and effective over time?
questions.answer: The city will need to ensure there is a dedicated team or partnership to continually update the app with real-time data and maintain accurate directories of available resources to meet the evolving needs of both first responders and the homeless population.

questions.question: What specific economic impacts are expected from the automation study at the Port of Long Beach?
questions.answer: The study aims to evaluate potential job displacement, changes in job quality, and overall economic effects on the local community, including impacts on small businesses that rely on port operations.

questions.question: How will the automation affect worker employment and wages in Long Beach?
questions.answer: Concerns are raised about the potential for reduced employment opportunities and lower-quality jobs replacing higher-paying longshoreman positions. Discussions are ongoing regarding maintaining or improving community wages amidst automation.

questions.question: What role will academic independence play in the study regarding automation at the port?
questions.answer: There is a strong emphasis on ensuring that the study is conducted independently and includes academic participation to provide unbiased and comprehensive analysis of automation impacts.

questions.question: How are you planning to balance automation with environmental concerns and community job retention?
questions.answer: Councilmembers expressed the need for the study to not only evaluate the economic implications of automation but also to ensure that environmental goals are met while safeguarding jobs and community welfare.

questions.question: What timeline and process were established for the council to receive the report on automation?
questions.answer: The council expects to receive a comprehensive report from the Port of Long Beach within 120 days, focusing on the scope, scale, and timeline regarding the impacts of automation.

questions.question: What are the anticipated ongoing maintenance costs for Sunnyside Cemetery after its transfer to the city?
questions.answer: The initial assessment indicates that the 13 acres of Sunnyside Cemetery would add approximately $230,000 of additional annual maintenance costs that are currently unbudgeted.

questions.question: What strategies are being proposed to enhance diversity recruitment within the Long Beach Fire Department?
questions.answer: The strategies proposed include hiring a full-time sworn diversity recruitment and partnership manager, implementing targeted outreach programs, conducting implicit bias training for staff, utilizing social media for recruitment efforts, developing a mentorship program, and partnering with educational institutions.

questions.question: How has the demographic makeup of fire department applicants changed over the years?
questions.answer: From 2014 to 2019, the percentage of black applicants for the Long Beach Fire Department has decreased from 15% to 8%, while Hispanic applicants have increased to levels similar to white applicants. Currently, only 5% of the department's sworn staff is female.

questions.question: What specific role does Councilmember Richardson want the city manager to explore in relation to diversity recruitment?
questions.answer: Councilmember Richardson is recommending that the city manager identify resources to establish a full-time sworn diversity recruitment and partnership manager position within the Long Beach Fire Department.

questions.question: What are the anticipated challenges in implementing the proposed recruitment strategies?
questions.answer: Challenges include identifying sustainable funding for the new recruitment position, overcoming implicit biases within current selection processes, and ensuring effective outreach to diverse communities to increase applicant pools.

questions.question: How will the success of the new diversity initiatives be evaluated?
questions.answer: The Long Beach Fire Department plans to implement pilot studies to measure the effectiveness of their recruitment strategies, utilize community surveys to assess perceptions, and continuously monitor and assess program outcomes to make necessary adjustments.

questions.question: What specific steps will be taken to address the challenges faced by the solid waste industry in Long Beach?

questions.answer: The inclusion of community hospital in the upcoming ballot measure is expected to ensure financial support for its reopening and operational costs, which is crucial for improving emergency transportation times and services for residents, particularly since ambulance transportation times have increased by 10% since its closure.

questions.question: What measures are in place to ensure the ongoing accountability and oversight of the funds raised from the proposed tax extension?

questions.question: What specific community benefits can residents expect from the measure if it is passed?

questions.question: How does the proposed tax extension compare to other local municipalities in terms of sales tax rates?

questions.question: In what ways can the current budget address the needs for infrastructure improvements, particularly for alleys and sidewalks?

questions.question: What steps is the city taking to involve residents in disaster preparedness efforts?
questions.answer: The city is promoting the 'Map Your Long Beach Neighborhood' program, which encourages residents to identify resources in their community and develop plans to help each other in the aftermath of a disaster. Residents can host meetings to discuss these plans, and the city is working with trained staff to facilitate these discussions.

questions.question: Are there any requirements for high-rise residential buildings to conduct earthquake drills?
questions.answer: Currently, there are no city or state regulations mandating earthquake drills for building owners of residential high-rises.

questions.question: How does the city plan to assess and update the inventory of seismically vulnerable buildings?
questions.answer: The city's next steps include hiring a consultant to inventory the vulnerable buildings and explore funding options to support retrofitting efforts. This initiative is aimed at establishing a proactive approach towards seismic safety as part of a comprehensive program.

questions.question: What role does the Alert Long Beach notification system play in disaster response?
questions.answer: The Alert Long Beach system is a mass notification system used to inform residents about emergencies, including earthquakes. Following recent seismic events, there was a significant increase in sign-ups for this alert system, highlighting its importance in community preparedness.

questions.question: What updates or improvements are being made to the city's infrastructure to enhance earthquake resilience?
questions.answer: The city is retrofitting critical facilities and ensuring new structures, like the new city hall, are designed to be earthquake-resilient. The infrastructure and building methods are being updated to improve resilience against seismic events, aiming to allow the city to remain operational even after a major earthquake.

questions.question: What specific strategies are being implemented to engage hard-to-count populations for the Census 2020, as mentioned in the presentation?
questions.answer: The city is focusing on creating a strategic outreach plan that includes partnerships with community-based organizations (CBOs) that are trusted messengers in hard-to-count areas. questions.question: How will the $322,141 in county funding be allocated between the city and community-based organizations (CBOs)?
questions.answer: At this stage, the amount allocated to support CBO outreach has not been finalized, as the city is still in the early planning phase. questions.question: What role do the community-based organizations (CBOs) play in the Census 2020 outreach efforts, and how is the city supporting them?
questions.answer: CBOs are crucial in reaching out to hard-to-count populations by leveraging their established trust within the community. questions.question: What measures are being taken to ensure that the materials used in the Census outreach are accessible and understandable to non-English speaking populations?
questions.answer: The initiative includes a requirement for a language access plan that mandates the translation of materials for the outreach campaign. This will ensure that the materials will be made available in multiple languages to effectively reach and educate non-English speaking residents.

questions.question: What adjustments were made to the tenant relocation ordinance since the last meeting?
questions.answer: There were discussions about tweaking the ordinance last time, but one speaker mentioned they had not heard back about any adjustments being made.

questions.question: How will the city ensure that tenants receive their relocation assistance before they are required to move?
questions.answer: There is a call for future amendments and a commitment to ensuring that tenants receive financial assistance in a timely manner, reflecting the spirit of the ordinance.

questions.question: What measures are being put in place to educate tenants and landlords about the new policy?
questions.answer: A robust outreach campaign is planned, which includes direct contact with property owners and providing information through the city's website and social media.

questions.question: What concerns do speakers have regarding the potential consequences of this ordinance on rent prices and tenant selection?
questions.answer: Some speakers expressed that making the policy overly stringent might lead landlords to raise rents or become too selective with tenants, potentially exacerbating the housing crisis.

questions.question: What data does the city have on how many landlords have raised rents following the ordinance's introduction?
questions.answer: Currently, staff indicated they do not have specific data on the number of landlords who have raised rents or the impact of the ordinance, but they agreed that tracking this data is important moving forward.

questions.question: What specific strategies were identified in the report to advance economic opportunity and inclusion in Long Beach?
questions.answer: The report identified five comprehensive recommendations which include establishing a municipal small business council, increasing procurement spending on local small businesses, expanding workforce development services at teen centers, supporting the establishment of a community development corporation, and promoting homeownership through HUD certified counseling programs.

questions.question: What challenges did the community members express regarding the current process of starting a business?
questions.answer: Community members highlighted obstacles such as difficulty in finding support and navigating bureaucratic processes, especially for non-English speakers and those unfamiliar with local resources.

questions.question: How did the community contribute to the formation of the implementation plan?
questions.answer: The community was engaged through a listening tour, focus groups, and nine community conversations that involved over 300 residents and business owners, providing input that shaped the recommendations.

questions.question: What is the significance of establishing a municipal small business council?
questions.answer: The small business council aims to provide representation, advocacy, and technical assistance for all small businesses in Long Beach, especially those outside established business districts, thereby fostering inclusivity and support.

questions.question: What specific measures can be taken to ensure that economic empowerment zones effectively benefit local communities rather than allowing outside investors to exploit them?
questions.answer: It is crucial to implement stringent requirements for businesses within these zones, such as hiring a significant percentage of local residents and ensuring that investments address the direct needs of the community, such as access to financial institutions and affordable housing.

questions.question: How will the city measure the success of the economic empowerment zone program over time?
questions.answer: Success can be measured through metrics such as increased local employment rates, business retention rates, improved access to essential services, and overall economic growth in the targeted neighborhoods.

questions.question: What concerns have residents expressed regarding potential displacement caused by the establishment of economic empowerment zones?
questions.answer: Residents have voiced worries that, without proper safeguards, the zones could attract outside investment that may lead to gentrification and displacement of long-term residents, emphasizing the need for policies that protect existing communities.

questions.question: In what ways can community feedback from past conversations shape the development of the economic empowerment zone program?
questions.answer: The community feedback collected in previous discussions will guide the specific features of the program, ensuring it addresses residents' needs such as access to capital, support for local businesses, and measures to prevent displacement.

questions.question: What examples from other regions could serve as a model for Long Beach's economic empowerment zone initiative?
questions.answer: Examples from places like Taiwan and India, which have successfully leveraged special economic zones to stimulate local growth and development, can provide insight on effective strategies to implement in Long Beach.

questions.question: What specific improvements and programs are being proposed for the 14th Street Park, and how will this benefit families in the Washington neighborhood?
questions.answer: The improvements proposed for 14th Street Park include children's empowerment programs and plans for building new homes nearby. These initiatives aim to enhance the overall quality of life for families and support community events, making the park a safer space for children and families.

questions.question: What role does Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles play in the revitalization efforts in the Washington neighborhood?
questions.answer: Habitat for Humanity is engaged in neighborhood revitalization efforts by building and rehabilitating homes, working on safe passage initiatives for students at Washington Middle School, and collaborating with local organizations and residents to improve the community.

questions.question: How can the council ensure that the identified funding, such as the $270,000 from Measure 2016, is utilized effectively for the community's needs?
questions.answer: The council can implement measures to track the progress of funded projects, involve community members in the planning and execution phases, and regularly assess the impact of improvements to align future funding with community needs.

questions.question: What additional support can the city provide to address the concerns raised by the residents regarding safety and accessibility in their neighborhoods?
questions.answer: The city can enhance public safety measures such as better lighting at crosswalks, increase community engagement in safety discussions, and fortify collaborations with local law enforcement to ensure that concerns about drug-related activities and pedestrian safety are adequately addressed.

questions.question: How will the program ensure equitable distribution of scooters in disadvantaged communities?
questions.answer: The program will require vendors to create a rate structure to ensure access for low-income residents, and the distribution of units will be managed by assigning a specific number of scooters to designated zones throughout the city.

questions.question: What measures are in place to manage abandoned scooters and ensure compliance with the program?
questions.answer: The program will include monitoring of scooter locations, requiring vendors to retrieve abandoned scooters and comply with the operational guidelines set by the city. The program also aims to maintain public safety and accessibility by ensuring scooters do not obstruct sidewalks or public spaces.

questions.question: Are insurance and liability requirements established for scooter operators?
questions.answer: Yes, vendors are required to carry insurance and liability coverage as part of their operational agreements with the city.

questions.question: What feedback mechanisms are in place for residents to report issues with scooters?
questions.answer: The city is considering re-establishing a call center for reporting problems with scooters, and there is also potential to integrate a reporting feature into the Go Long Beach app for abandoned scooters.

questions.question: How will the city ensure that operators comply with the established guidelines and reporting requirements?
questions.answer: All vendors will need to apply under the new permanent program guidelines and will be monitored for compliance. The city will assess permit applications based on adherence to program rules and performance metrics, including data on scooter usage and maintenance.
